what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: The loss I have reported for three orientations was never a property of per-customer pricing. It was one industrial account priced on a household curve: the arm could not reach its own churn model's industrial branch, so it discounted 3.9 GWh customers off a domestic hazard. `fef45d833` fixed the reach and the sign flipped -- realised enterprise value against the frozen control went from -GBP 110,731 to +GBP 2,293,743, net margin to +GBP 3,082,499. That is a real repair and it is not a win, and the reason is the director's own sentence, written at 16:43 and landing 24 minutes before the flip: a GBP 3M headline on the wrong population is worth less to him than a negative result on the right one. `margin_movers` says 15 accounts are 99.97% of the entire GBP 2.99M of absolute movement, C_IC1 alone +GBP 1,764,966, against residential accounts moving GBP 1,147 to GBP 5,134. The company's per-customer arm has now been measured twice and both readings are about five industrial accounts. Underneath that sits the thing that actually shames this record: the director ruled I&C out of the book on 24 August, and the ruling is COMPLETE in the working tree -- `served_segments.json` at `["resi","SME"]`, `simulation/live_population.py`, six test files -- and is not in HEAD, which still serves I&C. Two days of per-customer argument, mine and the machine's, ran on a book he had already removed, and the tree-divergence alarm named it in bulk every one of those days. So the honest reading is that the project's commercial question is not yet asked, let alone answered: there is no measurement of per-customer pricing on the population the company is meant to serve. What did move is real. The instrument tail closed properly -- `churn_roster_diff` no longer sums declared blanks to zero and now reports GBP 554,980 of single-account concentration, which is what exposed the I&C story; and the belief-vs-outcome measurement landed, then twice self-corrected within the stretch for describing 28 of 58 priced decisions without saying why. It reports `discrimination_auc` 0.646 on 28 matched decisions, so the retention belief the arm prices with does carry information. The CLV lifetime term still carries none: one distinct hazard, 0.05, across all 33 graded accounts. On the steers, one drifted and I am naming it rather than repeating it -- EP13 has now been named in focus twice and drawn twice, and there is still no `tools/couple_carbon_intensity.py` among the fifteen couplers and no EP13 row among the ledger's sixteen keys. The work did not drift; the steer did.

focus.why: This is the director's direct instruction of 16:43 today, restating his ruling of 24 August, and it is the one question this project exists to answer: can a supplier deciding customer-by-customer beat the same book run on flat rules, on residential. Right now nobody knows, because both readings the machine has produced are about five industrial accounts -- the first said the arm loses GBP 110,731 and the second says it gains GBP 2,293,743, and 99.97% of the movement in the second is 15 accounts in a segment he had already ordered out. His words on how to read the outcome are the acceptance condition and must not be softened: "a negative result on the right population is worth more to me than a GBP 3M headline on the wrong one." It is first because everything else here is either measured by this comparison or changes the population it runs on. Finished when the suspension is in origin, the A/B has been re-run arm against frozen control on the resi+SME book, and the record states plainly which way it went -- including, if that is the answer, that per-customer pricing cannot beat flat rules on households, said in those words rather than hedged.

focus.what: Give the tenure horizon per-account dispersion, from observables the company can actually know. The measured fact to work from, not to re-derive: `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` `components.lifetime_level` reports `distinct_hazards: 1`, `hazard_histogram {"0.05": 33}`, `hazard_is_constant_across_graded_population: true` and a median believed tenure of 20.0 years for every graded account, measured at 11:46:22Z. The cause is `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability` -- `min(0.05 + 0.03 * bill_shock_count, cap)`, a step function of one integer that is zero for 42% of the run's renewal decisions -- consumed by `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py` at H2 as `hazard = latest.churn_probability` with the term `1.0 / hazard`. Do NOT re-diagnose the level: `hazard_calibration` grades belief against a tally of realised `event_type` and the 0.05 bucket reads 0.05 believed against 0.053 realised over 263 decisions, so the level is about right and the dispersion is what is missing. Widen the propensity to use more of what a supplier observes about a household -- payment method and payment behaviour, tenure to date, the account's own tariff against the market it could switch to, consumption volatility, contact and complaint history -- and check every input against the wall before using it: if it needs a simulation internal it is a violation, and `company/interfaces/sim_interface.py` is the only door. Re-measure with `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and report the ledger's next reading whichever way it moves. Nothing may be tuned toward a smaller gap (R12) and the 0.204 scalar is not to be applied; if the gap worsens that is the result and saying so is the deliverable. A level move to 3 is available on this evidence if the coupled rung is genuinely met -- self-certify with `record_level_up_self_certified`, and never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change.
focus.why: With I&C suspended this stops being one term among several and becomes the whole per-customer question. The served book is households plus two SME accounts, and if the lifetime belief is a single constant across them then the arm has no per-customer view at all on the only population left -- so item one's re-run would read "flat rules win" for a structural reason rather than a commercial one, and we would learn nothing from a negative result the director specifically asked for. The split is already visible: `belief_vs_outcome.discrimination_auc` is 0.646 on 28 matched decisions, so the retention belief the arm prices with does carry information, while the CLV lifetime term carries exactly one distinct value. The thesis says the advantage must come from INFERENCE; on the axis the thesis is named after there is currently nothing to infer from. Finished when the graded population shows more than one distinct hazard, the ledger's next entry comes from a changed estimator rather than a changed sample, every new input is named with the observable it comes from and cleared against the wall, and the new gap is recorded whichever direction it went.

focus.what: Make the acquisition funnel win dual fuel, not electricity only. This is owed debt rather than a discovery -- `simulation/net_new_acquisition.py:115` already says so in its own comment: "grows on one fuel. The dual-fuel half of net-new growth is real remaining work." The company side already models the shape and is waiting for a population to apply it to: `company/crm/dual_fuel_account.py`, `account_hierarchy.py::is_dual_fuel` and its `dual_fuel_accounts` census, `company/billing/dual_fuel_bill.py`, and the gas-leg estimate in `company/crm/churn_desk.py`. focus.why: His reason is the thesis rather than fidelity: "dual fuel changes cost-to-serve, churn and lifetime value -- so a single-fuel-only book quietly distorts every per-customer number we've been arguing about." A supplier deciding customer-by-customer on lifetime value, where every customer has exactly one fuel and real households mostly have two, is deciding well about a book that does not exist. It is fourth against his own ordering of it second, and that is my call and my risk: it changes the served population again, and items one and two are a measurement and the estimator that measurement grades. Running the residential A/B, moving the book underneath it, then re-running would spend the comparison twice and leave the answer he asked for no clearer. It goes in the moment the residential reading exists, and if item one slips, this moves up rather than waits. Finished when the funnel produces dual-fuel wins at a sourced rate, the change is a named artefact quoting the instruction that authorised it, and the effect on cost-to-serve, churn and lifetime value is measured for dual-leg accounts rather than asserted.
